note: ADR-0006 template-owned path boundary. Ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix; a prefix ending in '/' matches a directory subtree, otherwise it matches an exact file. On a tie, user-owned wins (fail-closed: an upgrade never touches a path it isn't sure the template owns). Conservatively excludes apps/ (portal carries user/plugin pages) and infra/environments/ (per-instance config and secrets) for now; that boundary can widen later. services/api/migrations/versions/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned: Alembic migration files are an append-only, per-instance chain (each instance accumulates its own, chained by down_revision), so syncing them from the template breaks the instance's revision graph. It stays user-owned — the three-way merge must never rewrite an applied migration — but as of issue #198 `biffo core upgrade` runs a separate *additive* carry for it: new core migrations absent from the instance are appended, re-chained onto the instance's current head at upgrade time (and given a deterministic core_<hash> revision id if the template's own id is already taken in that instance), with the resulting chain validated for a single head before the PR is opened. Existing instance migrations are never modified, re-chained, or deleted. See cli/src/lib/core-migrations.ts. The migration framework itself (migrations/env.py, script.py.mako) stays template-owned. services/_plugins/ is template-owned even though services/ is user-owned: it is the carve-out that gives *first-party* plugins a distribution mechanism (issue #243). A plugin shipped in the template (e.g. orchestrator) previously sat directly under the user-owned services/, so `biffo core upgrade` fail-closed on it and the only channel left was manual PR copy-in — which is the absence of a mechanism, and let every instance's copy drift silently. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugins/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/api/ already does, so the underscore prefix (matching the existing services/_template/ convention, and un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name per registry-schema.json) is what declares ownership: a plugin under services/_plugins/ is the template's to maintain and is carried by every upgrade, while a third-party plugin installed into services/<name>/ stays the instance's and is never overwritten. Discovery (services/api/src/api/plugins.py) globs both locations, so the split is an ownership boundary only, never a runtime one. services/_plugin-host/ is template-owned for the same reason (ADR-0021): it is the shared plugin-host runtime the template maintains and every instance runs, so it needs a distribution channel or it drifts silently — the exact #243 failure. Without this carve-out `biffo core upgrade` fail-closes on it (services/ is user-owned), so the host Lambda provisioned by the template-owned infra/environments/dev/plugin-host.core.tf would ship but its code would never reach the instance, leaving it on the compute placeholder for ever. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugin-host/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/_plugins/ does; the underscore prefix (un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name) declares ownership. A plugin's own code stays under user-owned services/<name>/ and is mounted BY the host at deploy time (deploy-app.yml), never carried into the host source. services/pr-signer/ is template-owned for the same reason, and its own Terraform is split into infra/environments/dev/pr-signer.core.tf the same way plugin-host.core.tf carries the host's (issue #568). pr-signer is the isolated GitHub App credential holder for the endpoint control plane (ADR-0008) — platform/governance infrastructure every instance needs identically, not optional product code. It was left out of the original #243/#548 carve-out sweep: no code comment, ADR text, or manifest note anywhere ever stated a reason to exclude it, so this reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate choice, caught three weeks later by the same #243/#548 audit pattern run against it for the first time. Leaving it out meant a real post-launch fix — 0d97f5e ("fix(pr-signer): emit prettier-compatible JSON so permission PRs are minimal") — could ship in the template but never reach an already-scaffolded instance; only a manual PR copy-in could carry it, and nothing prompted anyone to do that. Unlike services/_plugins/ and services/_plugin-host/, the carved-out path is services/pr-signer/ without an underscore prefix: pr-signer is not a first-party member of the plugin system (it has no biffo.plugin.json, is not discovered by services/api/src/api/plugins.py, and is invoked over IAM directly rather than mounted by the plugin host), so it does not need the underscore convention's collision avoidance with a third-party plugin slug the same way those do. That leaves a narrow theoretical collision — a third-party plugin named exactly "pr-signer" — but the directory services/pr-signer/ already exists in every instance today regardless of this manifest entry, so `biffo plugin install` would already collide with it before this change; this carve-out changes who owns the bytes at that path, not whether the path is claimed. infra/environments/dev/pr-signer.core.tf is added to templateOwned alongside plugins.core.tf and plugin-host.core.tf for the same infra/environments/ carve-out reason (longest-prefix-wins over user-owned infra/); it carries the module "pr_signer" block, its Secrets Manager secret, and pr-signer's enable_pr_signer config-validation check block. It deliberately does NOT carry the invoke_function_arns argument or the BIFFO_PR_SIGNER_FUNCTION_NAME environment variable on module.core_api in main.tf — those stay on module.core_api's own block, which is not itself part of this carve-out, and they cross-reference module.pr_signer by name, which Terraform resolves regardless of which file in the directory declares the module. enable_pr_signer itself, and its pr_signer_github_app_id/pr_signer_github_installation_id/pr_signer_repo_owner/pr_signer_repo_name/pr_signer_base_branch companion variables, stay in the user-owned variables.tf: whether an instance runs the endpoint control plane at all, and which GitHub App/repo it targets, is legitimately per-instance policy, the same way enable_core_plugins stays user-owned policy layered on top of plugins.core.tf's template-owned wiring. apps/ is user-owned, but apps/portal/ within it is wholly template-owned (ADR-0006 longest-prefix wins). The portal is strictly the admin console (issue #306): it serves /admin and /login, the root path belongs to the user's application sibling, and nothing user-owned lives inside it. That portal code is a client of the Core API's admin surface — ~640 lines of *-api.ts calling /api/v1/admin/* — so it tracks the core API's version, not the instance's product. Leaving it user-owned meant template bugs in Biffo's own admin UI could not be distributed: #275 (navigation landing on the raw RSC payload) and #276 (login offering an unsupported identifier) both had to be hand-copied into every instance. #279 part 1 first tried this as a path-level carve-out (app/admin/, app/(auth)/, components/, lib/, context/), which was a trap: components/, lib/ and context/ are exactly where a user would put ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, and `core upgrade` would then propose deleting them. #306 removes the trap at its root by making the assumption explicit — the portal is not a canvas — rather than documenting around it, so the carve-out collapses to a single prefix. The instance's own product UI belongs in its application sibling repo, or in a NEW app under apps/, which stays user-owned by default. docs/ADR/ is user-owned: the template's ADRs are seeded once at `biffo init` as a starting point, but an instance's ADRs are its own decision record and legitimately diverge from the Biffo standard over time — force-syncing them on every core upgrade collides an instance's own ADR numbers with the template's and rewrites its history. Excluded from the sync flow for that reason; new template ADRs are announced in release notes rather than pushed into instances. _skeletons/ is template-owned (issue #325). It is scaffolding *source* — the trees `biffo init` (step 6/6), `biffo sibling create` and `biffo plugin create` copy from — not instance content, and no instance ever reads its own copy: the CLI resolves a skeleton by walking UP from its own module (defaultSiblingTemplateRoot() in cli/src/commands/sibling-create.ts, findSkeletonRoot() in cli/src/lib/plugin-scaffold.ts), so an npm-installed CLI lands on the copy packaged beside its own dist/ (cli/scripts/packaged-root-assets.mjs, #315), never on the instance's. The instance has a copy only because `biffo init` clones the whole template repo, and it has been frozen at init time ever since. Leaving it unowned was the #325 trap: cli/ IS template-owned, so the non-interactive-Terraform guard added in #322 (cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.ts) was distributed to every instance while the skeleton workflows it scans were not — every upgrade to 0.41.3 landed a guard whose subject the upgrade had no mechanism to fix, and instance CI went red on files the instance neither wrote nor could repair (reproduced on keiranholloway/biffo-platform PR #1). The general rule: a template-owned check must never assert over paths the template does not own. Same argument as services/_plugins/ (#243) — a path the template maintains needs a distribution channel, or it drifts silently in every instance, which is how the #322 bug survived unnoticed in the first place. This is NOT a repeat of the #279 part-1 trap: components/, lib/ and context/ were a trap because they are exactly where a user would put their own ProductCard.tsx or stripe.ts, whereas there is nowhere inside _skeletons/ a user would legitimately add a file. Customising the scaffold is done by pointing `biffo sibling create --template <path>` at your own tree — an explicitly supported flag — not by editing the inherited copy. Making it owned also re-syncs the template-owned tests that read it (cli/src/lib/secret-scan-scope.test.ts, cli/src/adapters/source-control/github/status-checks.test.ts) with their subject, and cli/src/lib/terraform-input-guard.test.ts now asserts every path the guard scans resolves as template-owned, so the mismatch cannot silently return. There is no core.version file to own since issue #423: the version the *template emits* is derived from its core-v* tags, so nothing in the tree names it and there is nothing to sync. The version an instance *received* is recorded in the userOwned biffo.core.json, which is what every lookup reads (cli/src/lib/core-version.ts). Issue #327 (audit follow-up to #325) swept the remaining template-owned checks that asserted over unowned paths and scoped each to template-owned code: the plugin-terraform guard (cli/src/lib/plugin-terraform-guard.ts) now filters discovered manifests through isTemplateOwned so a third-party plugin under user-owned services/<name>/ never reds a template-shipped gate; the CI infra-validate job fmt-checks and terraform-validates only modules/ (never user-owned infra/environments/, whose hardcoded dev env an instance may rename or remove); bandit runs over services/api and services/_plugins only (not the instance's own services/); ruff excludes _skeletons (matching pyright) and db/; and .prettierignore (now template-owned, so the scoping distributes) excludes the user-owned trees the format gate used to reach (apps/ except apps/portal, services/ except the template-owned services, infra/, docs/, README.md, biffo.* config). The general rule is encoded as an executable META guard in cli/src/lib/template-owned-scope.test.ts, with a negative control so it cannot pass by matching its own prose. pnpm-workspace.yaml's apps/* glob is left as-is: enrolling a new user app into the monorepo's shared lint/type/test is the point of a monorepo and the user opts in by creating the app there (the gate fires only on the user's own code, which the user can fix — not the #325 class where the subject is un-fixable inherited content). core-migrations.test.ts's real-tree single-head assertion is now skipped when biffo.core.json is present (i.e. in an instance), so it validates only the template's own shipped chain, never the instance's user-owned migrations/versions/. .githooks/commit-msg, .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are template-owned as EXACT FILES, not the .githooks/ directory (issue #370, moved there by #838). The hooks moved out of .husky/ because husky's runner directory .husky/_ is gitignored and generated only by `prepare` on `pnpm install`, while core.hooksPath is a RELATIVE path git resolves per worktree -- so every fresh worktree had no .husky/_ and git skipped every hook silently. Verified on tabsii-platform/.worktrees/discovery-rls, which carried the three tracked hook files, no .husky/_, and therefore no pyright, no lint-staged and no commitlint on any commit made there. A tracked hooks directory is present the instant a worktree exists, with no install step. The .husky/ files remain as forwarders for clones that have not re-run install since the upgrade and whose core.hooksPath still points at .husky/_; deleting them would disarm those clones silently, which is the failure being fixed. Same EXACT FILE reasoning as before: The template wires the hooks it ships -- commitlint, lint-staged, and the core-ownership guard -- and those wirings must reach instances or the guard exists only in the repo that does not need it. Owning the whole directory would be the #279 part-1 trap in another costume: an instance's own pre-push or post-merge hook is exactly the sort of file a user legitimately adds, and a template-owned subtree would propose deleting it. Exact-file entries own the two hooks the template actually writes and leave the rest of .husky/ to the instance. biffo.divergence.json is user-owned by the same reasoning as the other biffo.*.json files: it records which template-owned prefixes THIS instance knowingly diverges in (warn instead of block), which is per-instance policy the template must never overwrite -- and if it were template-owned, the guard would block the commit that configures the guard. infra/environments/dev/plugins.core.tf is template-owned even though infra/ is user-owned (longest-prefix-wins, same carve-out shape as apps/portal/ inside apps/): it provisions the first-party agentic plugins (orchestrator, agent-runtime) as core capability (ADR-0014), closing #406. The instantiation used to be hand-wired per instance in the user-owned main.tf and drifted — tabsii had it, a fresh instance had nothing and its agents were dead. Making just this file template-owned distributes the wiring and keeps every instance in parity, while leaving the rest of infra/environments/ (per-instance account/domain/secret config) user-owned. It depends only on the template-seeded shape every instance has (var.project_name, local.environment, local.tags, module.events, module.api_gateway) and passes the OpenRouter credential by SSM-path convention rather than a per-instance variable, so it upgrades cleanly into an older instance whose variables.tf never gained the plugin vars. The plugin-allowlist module's core_plugins default lists the same first-party set so those Lambdas reach /api/v1/internal/* with no edit to the user-owned root config; the two lists are kept in step (adding a first-party plugin touches both). .gitleaks.toml is template-owned as an exact file (#516), same reasoning as the .husky hooks (#370): the template ships the Secret Scan rules AND the code those rules must not flag, so it must be able to ship the allowlist that keeps them consistent — otherwise a template-shipped literal (e.g. the fck-nat vendor AMI-owner id, #514) reds every instance's Secret Scan on content the instance didn't write and can't diagnose (which is exactly what happened when the fck-nat module reached tabsii and biffo-platform). biffo core upgrade three-way-merges it, so a template rule/allowlist change distributes while an instance-added allowlist entry (a distinct line in the regexes/paths arrays) survives the merge; only a same-line edit conflicts. This is not the #279-part-1 trap: instance additions are preserved by the merge rather than proposed for deletion, and there is no place inside a shared scanner ruleset a user adds product code — product-specific allowlisting is an additive entry, not a competing file. modules/plugins/ is user-owned even though modules/ is template-owned (longest-prefix-wins), because `biffo plugin install` copies a THIRD-party plugin's terraform/ into modules/plugins/<name>/ (ADR-0003) — that copy is instance content the template will never ship, so an ownership guard marking it template-owned blocks the very install that writes it, and a core upgrade would propose deleting it. Same shape as a third-party plugin under user-owned services/<name>/. modules/plugins/_template/ is carved back to template-owned (a longer prefix still wins): it is the scaffold source `biffo plugin create` copies from, maintained by the template like _skeletons/, and rides core upgrade. First-party plugins are unaffected — their terraform lives in template-owned services/_plugins/<name>/ and is referenced in place (never copied into modules/plugins/). CI still terraform-validates modules/ (so a third-party plugin module is validated), and core upgrade simply never carries modules/plugins/<name>/. AGENTS.md is template-owned as an EXACT FILE (issue #559), same reasoning as CLAUDE.md (#370-class): it is the tool-agnostic rules of engagement CLAUDE.md imports (@AGENTS.md) and the single source of truth for agent/dev practice in every repo, so it must reach instances or it drifts silently -- which is exactly what happened and is what #559 is: tabsii's copy fell 68 lines behind the template's, missing the very workflow guardrails (masked-push detection, reproduce-the-bug-first, fresh-worktree-with-deps-sync discipline) the template had already written, because AGENTS.md was in neither ownership list and fail-closed to user-owned. Making it a templateOwned exact file (not the repo root, which stays user-owned) distributes it via biffo core upgrade like CLAUDE.md; the three-way merge preserves any genuine instance-specific addition while carrying template rule changes, and since the instances hold no such additions today (both were pure stale subsets of the template's) the first upgrade simply brings them current. Plugin and sibling repos are separate repos core upgrade never reaches, so they get AGENTS.md by vendoring it into _skeletons/plugin-template/ and _skeletons/sibling-template/ (every newly scaffolded repo) plus a one-time manual copy-in for existing ones -- the same distribution split every user-owned-repo artifact uses. CONTRIBUTING.md is template-owned for the same reason: it is a three-line pointer at AGENTS.md (no instance-specific content), so distributing it keeps every repo's contribution entry-point consistent rather than template-only. services/api/src/api/domains/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned (longest-prefix-wins, ADR-0022, issue #547): it is an instance's home for its OWN product-domain code (models, routers, events, schemas, tests) INSIDE the core API. ADR-0002 makes the core the single data plane -- the platform owns the data and applications are guests -- so a product's canonical relational domain belongs in the core DB/API by design (a sibling holds no DB per ADR-0007; a plugin owns no data per ADR-0003). But everything else under services/api/ is template-owned, so before this carve-out an instance could not edit its own domain code without the core-ownership guard blocking the commit and biffo core upgrade treating it as template drift (the exact snag that surfaced this: tabsii's tabsii.* schema and ~15 routers). This is the same shape as services/api/migrations/versions/ (user-owned inside template-owned services/api/): a longest-prefix-wins carve-out for legitimately-per-instance content. Discovery stays template-owned and distributes -- api.routing.domain_router globs domains/<name>/ and mounts each domain's exported routers, so main.py (template-owned) never needs a per-instance edit -- while the domains themselves are the instance's to maintain and are never carried by an upgrade. db/imports/<name>/ (DDL-imported schemas) is already covered: db/ is user-owned. The domains/ tree is seeded once (an __init__.py + README) like docs/ADR/, then owned by the instance; the base template ships no product domain, so build_domain_router mounts nothing there.
